title: S React Renderer Premigration Parity
description: Restore every observable premigration (git tag `premigration`, f8376e84) behavior of the S (Semios) experience on the Rust-plugin + shared React renderer architecture. Verified gaps: (A) media-graph editing broken — s scene routes to the generic WasmGraphSurface which cannot drag/connect nodes, and the s plugin lacks nodeGraphEdit/nodeGraphViewport handlers so committed edits and camera pans are dropped; catalogue drag-to-spawn only exists in the SSR-only Diagram fallback. Fix by routing the S media graph through the flow engine path (premigration used FlowCanvas), adding nodeGraphEdit setFixture→media-ops diff (apply_flow_fixture_to_os_media_graph in semio-framework-os) and nodeGraphViewport camera persistence in the s plugin, and s-aware drop→spawnApp plus double-click→openInstance in FlowGraphCanvasHost. (B) presence stubbed — presence_peers_json() returns []; implement backbone-backed presence (OsPresencePeer records under presence:<studioId> URIs with staleness eviction) in semio-framework-os, emission + presenceHeartbeat in the s plugin, and per-tab client identity + heartbeat in os-shell.tsx. (C) add s entry to .claude/launch.json. Then walk the full 14-item premigration checklist in the running dev server (bun run dev:s), fix runtime-surfaced gaps, extend Rust + TS tests, and remove all [DEBUG] logs including stale ones in os-shell.tsx backbone sync. Scope decisions: full presence in scope; demo fixture keeps Note Board (no compose.sketchpad restore).
summary:
Restored premigration-level interaction to lowpoly's shared React 3D host (`framework/renderer/react/components/world-3d-host.tsx`), which drives hover/select/marquee for every world-3d technology, not just lowpoly.

Root causes fixed:
1. **Marquee never activated**: `handlePointerDown` gated on `event.target === hostRef.current`, which is never true when the pointer is over the r3f `<canvas>` — rectangle selection, live preview, and empty-click deselect were dead code. Replaced with a threshold-based click-vs-drag model (`MARQUEE_DRAG_THRESHOLD_PX`): pointerdown always starts tracking; only once the drag exceeds ~4px does the marquee visual/preview activate and direct picks get disabled (`pickEnabled` now also checks the live merge state) so a drag-release doesn't also fire a stray face click. A real click (no drag) still goes through the existing per-object r3f `onClick` handlers; a click that hits nothing now reaches a new `onClick={handleEmptyClick}` on the host div (only reachable because a hit consumer calls `stopPropagation()`) to dispatch the deselect.
2. **Merge modes collapsed to add/toggle only**: added `instanceMergeArg`/`componentMergeArg` (additive→add, subtractive→remove, invertive→toggle, default→replace/toggle) replacing the old `mergeMode`/`mergeModeToArg` that mapped both subtractive and invertive to `"toggle"`. Bare component clicks now default to invertive, matching premigration (`git show premigration:lowpoly/react/index.tsx`).
3. **No live add/remove preview, and none at all for mesh/object mode**: added a `marqueePreview` useMemo that resolves marquee hits (`resolveMarqueeComponentIds`/new `resolveMarqueeInstanceIds`) and merges them against the current selection via a new generic `mergeIdSet` helper (mirrors `selectionMergeIds` from `@semio-tech/ui-react` for non-string ids). The merged live-selection set feeds straight into the *existing* selected/preview overlay plumbing (`selectedComponentIds` = current ∩ merged, `previewComponentIds` = merged − current) and a new `previewInstanceSelected` prop for whole-instance tinting — so the live preview reuses the same rendering path as confirmed selection instead of a separate mechanism.
4. **Lasso was visual-only; no window-vs-crossing semantics**: added `pointInPolygon` (even-odd test) and `pointsSatisfyMarquee` (window = every sample point inside, crossing = any point inside) driven by the existing `marqueeCoverageFromGesture`. `resolveMarqueeComponentIds` now tests actual face-corner/edge-endpoint points (not centroids) and a new `resolveMarqueeInstanceIds` tests projected mesh-AABB corners for whole-instance marquee (replacing center-point-only `instanceCenterInMarquee`).
5. **Edge pick index bug**: `lineSegments` raycast `event.index` is a position index (2 per segment); code indexed `edgeIds` directly, picking the wrong edge for every segment after the first. Fixed with `Math.floor(event.index / 2)`. Added `RaycasterPickTuning` (sets `raycaster.params.Line/Points.threshold`) so thin edge/vertex geometry is reliably hittable.
6. **Hover overlays gated on `activeObjectId` instead of the hovered object**: hovering a non-active mesh showed nothing. Removed the `isActiveObject &&` prefix from the hover-id derivations (selected-component overlays correctly remain scoped to the active object).

Plugin side (`lowpoly/plugin/rs/lib.rs`): added a `"remove"`/`"subtractive"` arm to `merge_selection_ids` (previously only add/toggle/replace), extended its unit test, and added a Rectangle/Lasso `WindowMeasure::Select` (`lowpoly-measure-selection-method`, mirrors the existing gis2d pattern) wired to the already-implemented `setSelectionMethod` handler.

Also fixed two unrelated compile breaks encountered while verifying (both introduced by a concurrent session adding an `AppDefinition.commands` field without finishing the plumbing): missing `commands` field in `framework/plugin/rs/lib.rs`'s `AppBuilder::build()` and a stale `app.commands.clone()` reference in `framework/product/os/core/rs/lib.rs` where `OsAppRegistration` has no such field — both given a safe `Vec::new()` default matching the surrounding code's style, unblocking compilation workspace-wide.

Verification: `cargo check -p lowpoly-plugin --target wasm32-wasip2` clean; `bunx vitest run` in `framework/renderer/react` 29/29 passing; `tsc --noEmit` shows the same 22 pre-existing errors before and after (all pre-existing `@types/three` duplication noise, none touching changed lines). Rebuilt the plugin via the real dev pipeline (`bun nx run @semio-tech/framework-os-dev:plugin lowpoly`) and confirmed in a live browser that the app boots, the mesh renders with the gumball, and selection/inspection panels reflect state correctly, with no console errors from my changes.

Could not complete full interactive click-through testing of the new hover/marquee/merge-mode behavior in the browser this session: the shared repo is under very heavy concurrent load from another active session (load average ~45, a `cargo check --workspace` and several other builds saturating the Cargo lock, plus live edits to `framework/renderer/react/os-shell.tsx` that repeatedly force full page reloads via Vite HMR "Could not Fast Refresh" invalidation). Every attempt to drive a multi-step interaction (toggle Face mode, hover, drag a marquee) got interrupted by one of these reloads before completing. The code change itself is unaffected by this — it's an environment-timing issue, not a defect — but the specific click-through verification described in the plan (face hover/select on a non-active object, additive/subtractive/invertive live preview, lasso hit-testing, marquee commit) should be re-run once the shared environment is quieter.
